items.recapEn: Tanaka-san waited on the steps of Seikenji, where trains run through the temple grounds, and ordered Hana and Ken to sit and drink. A sign said: do not enter, run or touch. They tried Shimizu-san's sour summer mikan; the real ones come in winter. Hana wrote they were getting used to the heat. Tanaka-san promised calm wind tomorrow.

items.recapEn: At Shimizu-san's roadside stand Hana tried a summer mikan and found it sour; Shimizu-san said the winter ones are far sweeter. Ken bought ten for cooking and swore his pack was lighter. Tanaka-san announced the time and found the shop clock a minute off. Shimizu-san promised to send Okitsu mikan in winter.

items.recapEn: The sign at the entrance to Seikenji: do not step into the stone garden, do not run on the old stones, do not touch the trees or flowers, do not feed the fish, no loud talking or packed lunches, and stop when a train comes. Then, more gently: drink water, rest on the steps, and we pray for your health.
